previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, chronic venous stasis ulcers, lipodermatosclerosis, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for worsening cellulitis around a left lower extremity ulcer. She presented with spreading erythema, pain, and drainage but no fever. IV vancomycin was initiated and continued throughout the hospitalization. A PICC line was placed to complete antibiotic therapy at home. Dermatology recommended discontinuing silver chloride on the ulcer due to potential irritation and advised diluted vinegar soaks followed by mupirocin and proper dressings. Imaging ruled out DVT, and asymptomatic bacteriuria was not treated. Her infection improved clinically, and she was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics and wound care, with follow-up planned with dermatology.

History of Present Illness:
Ms ___ is a ___ year old woman with a PMHx of 
lipodermasclerosis, recurrent lower extremity cellulitis, and 
chronic ulcers presents with increased redness, swelling, pain, 
drainage around left lower extremity ulcer. Patient was admitted 
___ for cellulitis, L lat malleolus wound w/ IV vanc; found 
to be MSSA and d/c'ed on clinda. She was off of antibiotics for 
about 2weeks before she was then readmitted to ___ with 
reoccurance of the cellulitis on ___ where a PICC line 
was placed and the patient was placed on IV vancomycin with 
improvement of the wound and was due to complete her course of 
antibiotics on ___ for a total of 10 days. She was unable 
to complete this regimen as the PICC line fell out. She reports 
that she had been doing well until over the 1 week prior to 
admission when she reported worsening of the cellulitis of the 
LLE (painful, red, not hot, edematous). Denies fevers, chills, 
abd pain, N/V, diaphoresis.
She was seen in clinic by her gerontologist ___ on 
the day prior to admission who noted that ""her left lower 
extremity skin condition has significantly worsened. The extent 
of erythema as well as severity have increased markedly. The 
redness is now extending into her right foot and also moving 
proximally up her calf. The drainage has been copious. Within an 
hour, she can saturate her dressing supplies. She has been 
putting on multiple 4x4 gauze pads as well as ABD padding with 
Kling wrap. She also has concerns regarding worsening pain and 
appearance of the lesion on her right ankle. Although there is 
currently no drainage, she has developed some mild erythema 
around the crusted area. There is another inferior area of 
crusting that also has her concerned. Although her right leg 
does not look nearly as concerning as her left, she says the 
pain is actually worse in her right ankle as compared with left 
leg."

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Left leg erythema and swelling

COMPARISON:  ___ 

FINDINGS: Grayscale and color Doppler sonographic evaluation was performed of
the left lower extremity.  Normal compressibility, flow and response to
augmentation is seen the left common femoral, superficial femoral and
popliteal veins.  Normal color Doppler flow is seen in the left peroneal and
posterior tibial veins.  

IMPRESSION: No left lower extremity DVT.

HISTORY:  Erythema and swelling of the left leg.

Six views of the left leg demonstrate marked subcutaneous edema which has
increased since ___.  There is no evidence of osteomyelitis,
fracture, subcutaneous gas, or bone destruction.  Incidental note is made of
tricomparmental osteoarthritis of the left knee, most severe in the medial and
patellofemoral compartments.  There are poorly visualized severe degenerative
changes at the naviculocuneiform articulation and a large plantar calcaneal
enthesophyte.

IMPRESSION: No evidece of osteomyelitis.

AP CHEST 5:15 P.M., ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with a new left PICC line.

IMPRESSION:
AP chest compared to ___:

New left PIC line crosses midline passing at least 7 cm into the right
brachiocephalic system.

Mild cardiomegaly and borderline vascular congestion are chronic.  No pleural
effusion.

Line placement corrected on subsequent chest radiograph.

AP CHEST 7:52 P.M. ON ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with cellulitis.  PICC line repositioned.

IMPRESSION:
AP chest compared to 5:15 p.m.:

Tip of the left PIC line is now in the mid SVC.  Mild cardiomegaly and
vascular congestion have improved.  Lungs grossly clear.  No pleural effusion.
